as_read: Conflicting with no clear benefit: the meta-analysis finds a small waist reduction with no effect on weight, BMI, appetite or metabolic measures and concludes it can't be recommended; a 1 g/day trial failed beyond placebo; some single trials are positive.

quote.text: Appetite parameters showed no significant changes and metabolic parameters did not improve with C.fimbriata supplementation therefore it is unlikely to recommend C. fimbriata as a weight loss supplement and an appetite suppressant.

proposed_decision_text: The 14 labels print Caralluma fimbriata extract at 815 or 1000 mg, two of them calling it bark extract and two sold as fat burners. This review read abstracts only. The evidence conflicts, with no clear benefit. A meta-analysis of 7 articles found waist circumference 1.59 cm lower and waist-hip ratio 0.06 lower against placebo, no significant effect on body weight, BMI or hip circumference, no significant change in appetite or biochemical measures, and concludes it is unlikely to recommend C. fimbriata as a weight loss supplement and an appetite suppressant (34758791). A trial of 500 mg twice daily in 89 overweight and obese patients found no result beyond placebo on anthropometry or appetite (25657901). Positive results exist and do not settle it. The stored trial of 1 g/day in 50 adults reports lower waist circumference and hunger against placebo, with weight, BMI and body fat not significantly different (17097761). A pilot of 1 g/day with waist circumference as its primary outcome reports 6.5 cm lost against 2.6 cm, with a printed interval of -7.466 to 0.228 that includes zero, in 33 analysed (23642949). A 16-week trial in 83 overweight adults, published after the meta-analysis search and with no dose in the abstract, reports weight maintained against gain on placebo (33762661). Outside weight, one trial reports lower anxiety and stress scores in 97 adults (30609411), and a crossover in 15 children with Prader-Willi syndrome reports eased hyperphagia (26713299).

stop_list: 34758791 gives no participant total in the abstract, so sample_size is left null rather than estimated
Two labels (330519, 330520) print bark extract; no abstract read describes bark, and 23642949 and 30609411 call the plant a succulent. Label wording only; not resolved here
clinician_items: 34758791: most common side effects reported were constipation, diarrhoea, nausea and rashes, reported by few studies.
stored_rating_note: positive_weak rests only on 17097761; the record does not reflect 34758791 or 25657901. Its text on non-significant weight, BMI and body fat matches the abstract.
unread_notes: Abstracts only. Search returned 20 and all were listed; no search result was left unlisted. Not opened: 31212875 (single case report), 41183620 (genus review), 33412248 (another species), and preclinical papers. 23876572 and 31793087 are broad reviews that name C. fimbriata favourably with no caralluma-only figures, and predate 34758791; 33650944 calls HPA effects unclear. First search on the bare word was swamped by MeSH mapping (8115 hits) and gave nothing used. 33762661's dose isn't in the abstract and full text was not opened.
